question: Choose the correct letter for the putamen
explanation: A is the putamen (lateral part of the striatum).

question: Choose the letter for the globus pallidus.
explanation: B is the globus pallidus (medial to the putamen).

question: Choose the letter for the caudate nucleus
explanation: A is the head of the caudate nucleus bulging into the lateral ventricle.

question: Choose the letter for the subthalamic nucleus
explanation: C is the subthalamic nucleus located superior to the substantia nigra.

question: A multiple sclerosis lesion could be found in which of the following structures
explanation: Multiple sclerosis is a demyelinating disease of the central nervous system (CNS). The medial lemniscus is in the brainstem (CNS), whereas cranial nerves outside the brainstem and spinal roots are part of the peripheral nervous system (PNS).

question: A patient who was diagnosed with relapsing-remitting MS several years ago is likely to have which of the following features present in their MRI?
options: demyelinating plaques at the surface of gyri
demyelinating plaques at margins of lateral ventricles
correctAnswer: demyelinating plaques at margins of lateral ventricles
explanation: MS characteristically presents with periventricular demyelinating plaques (Dawson fingers) radiating around the lateral ventricles.

question: Choose the correct letter for the Superior Cerebellar Peduncle
explanation: D points to the superior cerebellar peduncle (brachium conjunctivum) forming the lateral wall of the 4th ventricle.

question: Choose the letter for the Pontine Nuclei.
explanation: H indicates the pontine nuclei scattered among the longitudinal corticospinal fibers in the basilar pons.

question: Choose the letter for the Middle Cerebellar Peduncle
explanation: H is the massive middle cerebellar peduncle (brachium pontis) carrying pontocerebellar fibers.

question: Choose the letter for the nodulus
explanation: B is the nodulus, the midline component of the flocculonodular lobe.

question: Choose the letter for the Dorsal Spinocerebellar Tract
explanation: K is the dorsal spinocerebellar tract (DSCT) located on the dorsolateral margin of the spinal cord.

question: Choose the letter for the Decussation of the Superior Cerebellar Peduncle
explanation: D is the decussation of the superior cerebellar peduncles in the caudal midbrain tegmentum.

question: Choose the letter for the inferior cerebellar peduncle
explanation: F is the inferior cerebellar peduncle (restiform body) on the dorsolateral medulla.

question: Choose the letter for the Dentate Nucleus
explanation: N is the dentate nucleus, the largest and most lateral deep cerebellar nucleus.

question: A patient who has a lesion involving the cerebellar vermis would have which of the following symptoms
options: inaccurate pointing to targets with an upper limb
intention tremor of a lower limb movement
explanation: The cerebellar vermis coordinates midline and axial body posture; lesions cause truncal ataxia and difficulty with tandem walking.

question: An MS plaque that occurs in the frontopontine fibers on the right side would cause which of the following symptoms?
options: weakness on the left side of the body
limb ataxia on the right side
limb ataxia on the left side
correctAnswer: limb ataxia on the left side
explanation: Right frontopontine fibers project to right pontine nuclei, which cross to the left cerebellum via the middle cerebellar peduncle. Since the left cerebellum coordinates the left limbs, a lesion of the right frontopontine pathway causes left limb ataxia.

question: Choose the letter for the position of frontopontine fibers
explanation: K represents the medial portion of the crus cerebri carrying frontopontine fibers.

question: A lesion located in the pontine nuclei on the left side would cause which of the following symptoms
options: weakness on the right side of the body
slowed movement; tremor on the right side of the body
limb ataxia of limbs on the left side
limb ataxia on the right side
correctAnswer: limb ataxia on the right side
explanation: Left pontine nuclei project across the midline to the right cerebellar hemisphere, which coordinates the right limbs. A left pontine lesion therefore causes right limb ataxia.

question: A lesion at the location indicated by B in the accompanying picture would cause which of the following symptoms
explanation: B is the nodulus (vestibulocerebellum); lesions disrupt vestibular coordination of eye and balance control, resulting in nystagmus.

question: Identify the structure labeled "A" in the accompanying picture.
explanation: A is the flocculus of the cerebellum.

question: Choose the letter for the position of superior cerebellar peduncle fibers
explanation: M designates the position of superior cerebellar peduncle fibers traversing the red nucleus in the rostral midbrain.

question: Tumors can be identified as meningiomas in MRI/CT images by their
explanation: Meningiomas are extra-axial dural-based tumors that characteristically display a dural tail sign on contrast MRI/CT.

question: Which of the following would be a diagnostic feature of a vestibular schwannoma?
explanation: Vestibular schwannomas characteristically show alternating Antoni A (dense with Verocay bodies) and Antoni B (hypocellular) patterns.

question: A pathologist's analysis of a biopsy specimen taken from a patient (shown in the picture) indicated the tumor was a glioblastoma multiforme. What feature of the specimen helped to make this diagnosis?
explanation: Glioblastoma multiforme (WHO grade IV) histologically features pseudopalisading necrosis and microvascular proliferation.

question: The picture below is a specimen from a tumor. Based on it's histological features, this tumor is best identified as
explanation: Oligodendrogliomas are characterized by cells with round nuclei and clear perinuclear halos ('fried egg' appearance) with a 'chicken-wire' capillary network.

question: Which of the following deficits is characteristic of a patient that has a medulloblastoma?
options: deviation of the tongue on protrusion
weakness on one side of the body
explanation: Medulloblastoma commonly originates in the cerebellar vermis in children, presenting with truncal and gait ataxia.

question: Which of the following is a feature of NF2?
explanation: Neurofibromatosis type 2 (NF2) is characterized by bilateral vestibular schwannomas (acoustic neuromas).

question: HSV-1 encephalitis would be expected to cause a lesion in the
explanation: HSV-1 encephalitis has a strong predilection for the temporal lobes and inferior frontal lobes.

question: A patient who has a vesicular rash restricted to a single dermatome on the body most likely has
explanation: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) reactivation causes shingles (herpes zoster), producing a painful vesicular rash restricted to a single dermatome.

question: Which of the following is a feature of rabies virus infection?
options: entry of the virus directly into spinal cord from the skin
the virus enters the brain from the blood supply
cowdry type A inclusions in brain neurons
negri bodies in cytoplasm of brain neurons
correctAnswer: negri bodies in cytoplasm of brain neurons
explanation: Rabies virus infection is pathognomonic for eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusion bodies known as Negri bodies in pyramidal and Purkinje neurons.

question: Which of the following is a diagnostic feature of toxoplasmosis infection?
options: demyelination of white matter in cerebral hemispheres
explanation: Toxoplasmosis typically produces multiple ring-enhancing lesions on MRI with a predilection for the basal ganglia in immunocompromised patients.

question: An immunocompromised patient was diagnosed with progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy. Which of the following features would support this diagnosis?
options: demyelination of white matter in cerebral hemispheres
correctAnswer: demyelination of white matter in cerebral hemispheres
explanation: PML (caused by JC virus infecting oligodendrocytes) causes multifocal demyelination of subcortical white matter in cerebral hemispheres.

question: The india ink stain is a laboratory test that can be used to diagnose which of the following disorders?
explanation: India ink preparation reveals the prominent clear polysaccharide capsules of Cryptococcus neoformans in cerebrospinal fluid.

question: Choose the correct letter for the Middle Cerebral Artery
explanation: A is the middle cerebral artery (MCA) coursing laterally into the lateral sulcus.

question: Choose the letter for the Basilar Artery.
explanation: C is the basilar artery ascending on the anterior surface of the pons.

question: Choose the letter for the Anterior Cerebral Artery
explanation: B is the anterior cerebral artery (ACA) heading anteromedially into the longitudinal fissure.

question: Choose the letter for the Vertebral Artery
explanation: D is the vertebral artery ascending toward the pontomedullary junction.

question: What structure emerges between the posterior cerebral artery and superior cerebellar artery?
explanation: The oculomotor nerve (CN III) emerges in the interpeduncular cistern between the posterior cerebral artery (PCA) and superior cerebellar artery (SCA).

question: Choose the letter for the Posterior Cerebral Artery (use the answer to #5 to help)
explanation: F is the posterior cerebral artery (PCA), passing superior to CN III.

question: Choose the letter for Broca's area.
explanation: H is Broca's area (pars opercularis and pars triangularis of the inferior frontal gyrus).

question: A patient who can understand commands spoken to them and can speak normally but cannot repeat sentences told to them has which disorder?
explanation: Damage to the arcuate fasciculus disrupts repetition while preserving fluency and comprehension, defining conduction aphasia.

question: Choose the letter for Wernicke's area
explanation: D designates Wernicke's area (receptive language region at the temporoparietal junction).

question: A patient who cannot speak but understands commands spoken to them probably has a lesion related to
options: anterior part of the paracentral lobule
explanation: Broca's expressive aphasia (intact comprehension with impaired speech production) is typically caused by a superior division MCA stroke.

question: An MS plaque that occurs in the arcuate fasciculus would cause which of the following symptoms?
options: loss of tactile sensation on one side of the body
weakness on one side of the body
explanation: An MS plaque affecting the arcuate fasciculus disconnects Wernicke's and Broca's areas, causing conduction aphasia.

question: Choose the letter for the Posterior Communicating Artery
explanation: 27 is the posterior communicating artery connecting the internal carotid to the posterior cerebral artery.

question: Choose the letter for the Anterior Spinal Artery
explanation: 13 is the anterior spinal artery descending along the ventral surface of the medulla and spinal cord.

question: Which of the following symptoms is an example of a focal neurological deficit?
options: weakness of the right upper limb
correctAnswer: weakness of the right upper limb
explanation: Weakness of the right upper limb is a focal neurological deficit attributable to a discrete lesion in the contralateral motor system.

question: Which of the following areas is supplied by the anterior circulation of the brain?
explanation: The primary motor cortex is supplied by the anterior circulation (internal carotid system via ACA and MCA).

question: The most common cause of occlusion of small cerebral vessels is
explanation: Lipohyalinosis and microatheroma are the primary pathological mechanisms underlying small penetrating vessel occlusion (lacunar strokes).

question: Which of the following is the most important risk factor for thrombotic stroke?
explanation: Hypertension is the single most important modifiable risk factor for thrombotic and ischemic stroke.

question: The lesion shown in the left hemisphere of the following image, is best characterized as
explanation: The small, discrete hyperintensity in the internal capsule on DWI represents an acute lacunar infarct.

question: The type of image shown in the previous question identifies small pathological areas more reliably? What type of image is it?
explanation: Diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI) is the most sensitive imaging modality for detecting acute ischemia and small lacunar infarcts.

question: The most common location for subarachnoid hemorrhage is
explanation: Subarachnoid hemorrhages most commonly arise from ruptured saccular (berry) aneurysms in the Circle of Willis.

question: The first step in treating a stroke patient is
options: determine if the cause is thrombosis or embolis
determine the location of the lesion
rule out hemorrhage as the cause
correctAnswer: rule out hemorrhage as the cause
explanation: The urgent first step in acute stroke evaluation is non-contrast CT to rule out intracranial hemorrhage before thrombolytic therapy.

question: Considering the relationship between mean arterial pressure and cerebral blood flow (CBF)
options: CBF is directly proportional to mean arterial pressure
CBF is independent of mean arterial pressure over a broad range
CBF decreases with increases in mean arterial pressure
CBF is not affected by mean arterial pressure
correctAnswer: CBF is independent of mean arterial pressure over a broad range
explanation: Cerebral autoregulation maintains constant cerebral blood flow (CBF) independent of mean arterial pressure across the range of approximately 60-150 mmHg.

question: The degenerative changes caused by excitotoxicity involve
options: high levels of ATP in damaged tissue
low levels of glutamate synthesis in damaged neurons
high levels of oxygen from loss of CBF autoregulation
inhibition of GABA receptors in hypoxic tissue
explanation: Glutamate excitotoxicity triggers massive influx of Ca++ through NMDA receptors, activating apoptotic and necrotic pathways.

question: Which of the following are included as criteria to establish a diagnosis of brain death
options: loss of function of at least one cerebral hemisphere
an unknown cause if the EEG is silent
explanation: Brain death criteria require irreversible cessation of all brainstem function (including absence of brainstem reflexes and apnea).

question: Which blood vessel supplies the area for UMNs for the leg
explanation: The leg/lower limb representation in the primary motor homunculus is along the medial hemisphere surface, supplied by the anterior cerebral artery (ACA).

question: Occlusion of which blood vessel would cause homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing.
explanation: Occlusion of the posterior cerebral artery (PCA) causes contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing due to collateral MCA supply at the occipital pole.

question: Which blood vessel supplies the hypoglossal nucleus and nerve.
explanation: The hypoglossal nucleus and exiting nerve fibers in the medial medulla are supplied by the anterior spinal artery (ASA).

question: Occlusion of which blood vessel would result in inability to understand words and spoken commands .
explanation: Wernicke's area in the superior temporal gyrus is supplied by the inferior division of the middle cerebral artery (MCA).

question: Which blood vessel supplies nucleus ambiguus.
explanation: Nucleus ambiguus in the lateral medulla is supplied by the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA; lateral medullary syndrome).

question: Occlusion of which blood vessel would result in thalamic pain syndrome.
explanation: Thalamic pain syndrome (Dejerine-Roussy) results from infarction of the sensory thalamus (VPL/VPM) supplied by thalamogeniculate branches of the PCA.

question: Which blood vessel supplies the corticospinal tract in the spinal cord.
explanation: The lateral corticospinal tracts in the spinal cord are situated in the anterior two-thirds of the cord supplied by the anterior spinal artery (ASA).

question: Occlusion of which blood vessel would result in loss of the pupillary light reflex, dilated pupil, and eye turned down and out all in the left eye.
explanation: CN III palsy (dilated, 'down and out' pupil) occurs with PCA or PCoA aneurysms or PCA vascular lesions in the midbrain.

question: A branch of this blood vessel forms the central retinal artery.
explanation: 34 is the internal carotid artery, which gives off the ophthalmic artery; the ophthalmic artery gives rise to the central retinal artery.

question: A branch of this blood vessel results in UMN deficits on one side of the body without any sensory deficits.
explanation: 31 is the middle cerebral artery trunk; its lenticulostriate branches supply the posterior limb of the internal capsule, causing pure motor stroke.

question: Choose the correct letter for the Mammillary Bodies
explanation: E points to the mammillary body at the base of the hypothalamus.

question: Choose the letter for the Fornix.
explanation: G is the column of the fornix.

question: Choose the letter for the Hippocampus
explanation: F is the hippocampus in the medial temporal lobe.

question: Choose the letter for the Amygdala
explanation: F is the amygdala in the anterior medial temporal lobe.

question: Choose the letter for the splenium of corpus callosum
explanation: F is the splenium of the corpus callosum (posterior thickened end).

question: Identify the structure labeled F
explanation: F is the body/columns of the fornix beneath the corpus callosum.

question: Identify the structure labeled G
explanation: G is the amygdala in the anterior medial temporal region at this coronal level.

question: Identify the structure labeled G
explanation: G is the hippocampus in the parahippocampal region.

question: Identify the structure labeled K
explanation: K points to the mammillary body on the midsagittal brain surface.

question: Choose the letter for the fornix
explanation: H is the fornix arching below the corpus callosum.
